### Pattern 3: Dependency Injection (Inversion of Control)
**When:** Any time a class needs an external dependency
**Why:** Enforces the dependency rule — high-level modules don't depend on low-level modules

```typescript
// ❌ WRONG: Hard-coded dependency (breaks dependency inversion)
class CreateOrderUseCase {
  private repo = new PrismaOrderRepository()  // depends on infrastructure!
}

// ✅ RIGHT: Constructor injection (depends on interface, not implementation)
class CreateOrderUseCase {
  constructor(private readonly repo: OrderRepository) {}  // interface, not impl
}
```

---

### Pattern 4: Result/Either Pattern for Error Handling
**When:** Operations that can fail in domain-predictable ways
**Why:** Forces callers to handle errors explicitly; avoids exception-based control flow in business logic

```typescript
// ❌ WRONG: Throw exceptions for business logic errors
class Order {
  applyDiscount(code: string): void {
    if (!this.isValidCode(code)) throw new InvalidDiscountError()
  }
}

// ✅ RIGHT: Return Result type
type Result<T, E> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }

class Order {
  applyDiscount(code: string): Result<Order, 'INVALID_CODE' | 'EXPIRED'> {
    if (!this.isValidCode(code)) return { ok: false, error: 'INVALID_CODE' }
    return { ok: true, value: this.withDiscount(code) }
  }
}
```

### Anti-Pattern 2: Anemic Domain Model
**Problem:** All business logic lives in services, entities are just data bags. Domain layer becomes meaningless.

```typescript
// ❌ WRONG: Entity is just a data container
class Order {
  id: string
  status: string
  items: OrderItem[]
  total: number
  // No behavior — just getters/setters
}

// ❌ WRONG: All logic in service (anemic model)
class OrderService {
  cancelOrder(order: Order): void {
    if (order.status === 'SHIPPED') throw new Error('Cannot cancel shipped order')
    order.status = 'CANCELLED'  // direct mutation
  }
}

// ✅ RIGHT: Rich domain model — entity owns its rules
class Order {
  private constructor(
    private readonly id: OrderId,
    private status: OrderStatus,
    private items: ReadonlyArray<OrderItem>
  ) {}

  cancel(): Result<Order, 'CANNOT_CANCEL_SHIPPED'> {
    if (this.status === OrderStatus.SHIPPED) {
      return { ok: false, error: 'CANNOT_CANCEL_SHIPPED' }
    }
    return { ok: true, value: new Order(this.id, OrderStatus.CANCELLED, this.items) }
  }
}
```

---

### Anti-Pattern 3: Infrastructure Leaking into Domain
**Problem:** Framework/DB imports in domain layer — makes domain untestable and creates tight coupling

```typescript
// ❌ WRONG: Prisma (infrastructure) inside domain entity
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'  // infrastructure!
class OrderRepository {
  async find(id: string): Promise<Order> {
    return prisma.order.findUnique({ where: { id } })
  }
}

// ✅ RIGHT: Pure interface in domain, implementation in infrastructure
// domain/repositories/OrderRepository.ts (interface — no imports)
interface OrderRepository {
  findById(id: OrderId): Promise<Order | null>
  save(order: Order): Promise<void>
}

// infrastructure/persistence/PrismaOrderRepository.ts (implementation)
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
class PrismaOrderRepository implements OrderRepository {
  async findById(id: OrderId): Promise<Order | null> { /* Prisma query */ }
  async save(order: Order): Promise<void> { /* Prisma write */ }
}
```

## Testing Strategy (Architecture-Aligned)

| Layer | Test Type | Dependencies | Pattern |
|-------|-----------|-------------|---------|
| Domain | Unit | None (pure functions) | Test domain logic in isolation |
| Application | Unit | Mock ports/interfaces | Inject mock repositories |
| Infrastructure | Integration | Real DB / external | Test against real infrastructure |
| E2E | E2E | Full stack | Test user-visible workflows |

```typescript
// Domain layer test — no mocks needed (pure logic)
describe('Order', () => {
  it('cannot be cancelled after shipping', () => {
    const order = Order.create({ status: OrderStatus.SHIPPED, ... })
    const result = order.cancel()
    expect(result.ok).toBe(false)
    expect(result.error).toBe('CANNOT_CANCEL_SHIPPED')
  })
})

// Application layer test — mock the repository port
describe('CreateOrderUseCase', () => {
  it('creates order and emits event', async () => {
    const mockRepo: OrderRepository = { save: jest.fn(), findById: jest.fn() }
    const useCase = new CreateOrderUseCase(mockRepo)
    await useCase.execute({ userId: 'u1', items: [...] })
    expect(mockRepo.save).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ status: 'PENDING' }))
  })
})
```

## Decision Checklist
Before writing any new code, verify:
- [ ] Is this in the correct layer (domain / application / infrastructure)?
- [ ] Does it respect the dependency rule (no upward imports)?
- [ ] Does it follow naming conventions for its type?
- [ ] Is domain logic in domain objects (not in services)?
- [ ] Are infrastructure dependencies injected (not hard-coded)?
- [ ] Is it testable without the framework or database?
